name: a_global_fx_metals
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Global, FX, metals.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
DXY, USD/JPY, EUR/USD; gold, silver, copper (price, % change); ECB, BoE, BoJ, PBoC actions and quotes; Europe/Asia index moves overnight into the brief date.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.

## Gold `[Macro / Commodities]`

- COMEX gold rose 2.06% overnight into Oct. 16; the source did not provide a price or exact ET timestamp (Shanghai Metals Market, Oct. 16, publication time not reported).[2]
- Spot gold traded at $4,155.55 per ounce, down 0.4%, at 05:50 local time in the source; that timestamp is after the 02:03 ET cutoff and is out of scope (ET Now, Oct. 16, publication time not reported).[7]

## Silver `[Macro / Commodities]`
- COMEX silver rose 3.09% overnight into Oct. 16; the source did not provide a price or exact ET timestamp (Shanghai Metals Market, Oct. 16, publication time not reported).[2]
- Spot silver was $57.16, down 0.5%, at 05:50 local time in the source; that timestamp is after the 02:03 ET cutoff and is out of scope (ET Now, Oct. 16, publication time not reported).[7]

## Copper `[Macro / Commodities]`
- LME copper fell 1.25% overnight into Oct. 16; the source did not provide an exact ET timestamp or dollar price for that reading (Shanghai Metals Market, Oct. 16, publication time not reported).[2]
- Three-month LME copper was $14,347 per metric ton and described as flat during the Oct. 16 Asian session; the source did not provide an exact ET timestamp (Saxo, Oct. 16, publication time not reported).[8]

## Europe `[Macro / Global Equities]`
- The pan-European STOXX 600 fell 0.16% to 636.73 at 09:01 GMT on Oct. 15, equivalent to 05:01 ET; European regional indexes were mixed at that time (Reuters, Oct. 15, publication time not reported).[4]
- European stocks finished 0.38% higher on Oct. 15; the report did not provide an exact ET timestamp (Reuters, Oct. 15, publication time not reported).[1]

## Asia `[Macro / Global Equities]`
- South Korea’s KOSPI plunged almost 8% on Oct. 15, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell nearly 5%; the report did not provide exact closing levels or ET timestamps (Reuters, Oct. 15, publication time not reported).[1]
- The MSCI Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan fell 3.12% on Oct. 15, its largest one-day decline since late July; the report did not provide an exact ET timestamp (Reuters, Oct. 15, publication time not reported).[1]
- Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 4.8% to 64,489.06 during Oct. 15 trading; the source did not provide an exact ET timestamp (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, publication time not reported).[6]
- South Korea’s KOSPI rose almost 3% during early Oct. 16 Asian trading after its Oct. 15 decline; the source was published at 03:05 ET, after the 02:03 ET cutoff, so the report is out of scope (Bloomberg, Oct. 16, 03:05 ET).[3]
